 El Aynaoui looking ahead to Essen with confidence and “full focus” 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Not even the cold, wet autumn weather in Leipzig could dampen Neil El Aynaoui’s spirits. “I played in northern France too, so I’m used to this weather,” he joked after the Red Bulls’ open recovery session.
 And there was another reason to be cheerful. “ You always feel better after a win ,” he said with a laugh as he spoke to the media on Sunday morning .
 OneFootball Videos
 A regular in the starting XI
 Our summer signing, who joined RBL from AS Roma on deadline day, was once again in the starting line-up for Saturday’s 4-0 home win over Elversberg . It’s become a familiar sight: El Aynaoui has started all nine of his appearances for the Red Bulls so far, completing the full 90 minutes on six occasions. He also registered his first assist for the club in the 6-0 thrashing of Eintracht Frankfurt .
 The Moroccan has quickly established himself as a key player thanks to his performances both on and off the ball, whether playing as a number eight or in a deeper role as a number six. However, he admits he’s still adjusting to the Bundesliga. “ I still need a bit more time to adapt . Football is played very differently in Germany compared to France or Italy.”
 His teammates have been a big help in that respect, both on and off the pitch. “The players alongside me in midfield make my job easier. When you’re playing with high-quality players , everything becomes less taxing,” he said in praise of his teammates.
 Pressure? “It’s always there”
 The 25-year-old World Cup participant believes there’s still more to come, both from himself and the collective team. Expectations are high at RBL, but El Aynaoui is no stranger to pressure. “ There’s always pressure in football , and you need it to perform at your best. We try to deal with it,” he explained.
 The midfielder has also identified areas where the team can improve. “We need to keep getting better, particularly when it comes to pressing and playing together as a team . That’s what we’re working on.”
 Neil wary of Essen
 The Red Bulls will be looking to put that work into practice away from home. While RBL have been winning game after game at the Red Bull Arena , results on the road have been less convincing. “When we play at home in front of our fans, we seem to give that little bit extra in every area. Now we need to find solutions so we can perform just as well away from home,” he said.
 The next opportunity comes on Tuesday, when RBL travel to Rot-Weiss Essen in the second round of the DFB-Pokal , where a tough cup tie awaits. “To be honest, I don’t know much about them. But I know there are no easy games in the DFB-Pokal ,” El Aynaoui said ahead of the trip.
 His previous experiences have taught him not to underestimate lower-league opposition. “In France, we sometimes played against teams from the third or fourth division, and those games can actually be even more difficult. We need full focus .”
